question.text: Which of these western US cities will have Tesla Robotaxi service on December 31, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the availability status of Tesla Robotaxi service for Las Vegas, NV and Phoenix, AZ as of December 31, 2026 (i.e., using the most recent information before January 1, 2027) according to [Tesla's Robotaxi](https://www.tesla.com/robotaxi) information portal. A city listed as "Coming soon" does not count.
question.fine_print: If the main resolution source does not provide the information on the target date, other credible sources such as the [Robotaxi support page](https://www.tesla.com/support/robotaxi#availability) or credible sources may be used.

research:
## Research summary: Tesla Robotaxi in Phoenix and Las Vegas by Dec 31, 2026

As of mid-November, Tesla is not running public Robotaxi rides in either city. Both are listed as "Coming soon", which does not count for resolution. I could not load Tesla's own pages, so this status comes from third-party trackers.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-17: Both tesla.com/robotaxi and tesla.com/support/robotaxi returned HTTP 403 when I tried to fetch them, so I could not check the live status myself. [tesla.com/robotaxi](https://www.tesla.com/robotaxi)
- 2026-11-09 (the date the tracker checked its data): The tracker says Tesla's site has listed Phoenix, Las Vegas and Jacksonville as "Coming soon" since 2026-10-21, with no launch dates. Live cities: Austin, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, Houston, Dallas, Fort Worth, San Antonio and the SF Bay Area. [ChargePort tracker](https://thechargeport.com/robotaxi-tracker)
- Another tracker agrees: Phoenix is at "Preparations Underway" and Las Vegas at "Announced", and neither is live. This tracker is run by an accessories retailer and contradicts itself in places. [Basenor tracker](https://www.basenor.com/pages/tesla-robotaxi-tracker)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Wikipedia lists Las Vegas as "Approved, not launched" and Phoenix as "Service announced". [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi)
- I found no reports of public Tesla Robotaxi rides in either city up to 2026-11-17.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Miami's service area doubled to about 59 sq mi. Cybercab orders opened, with deliveries from December, limited to certain service areas. This shows Tesla is still expanding, but neither item is about Phoenix or Las Vegas. [Teslarati](https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-doubled-miami-robotaxi-geofence/), [Motor1](https://www.motor1.com/news/815563/tesla-cybercab-robotaxi-limits/)
- 2026-11-11: Tesla posted that Robotaxi "now runs 24/7" in the cities where it is available. [ChargePort](https://thechargeport.com/robotaxi-tracker)
- 2026-11-09: San Antonio went live, 19 days after Tesla named it alongside Las Vegas, Phoenix and Jacksonville. Fort Worth went live 2026-11-02. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi)
- 2026-10-21: On the Q3 earnings call, Tesla said Cybercab rides would start in Dallas in November and that more cities could follow "towards the end of the year". It named no Phoenix or Las Vegas dates. Tesla's Safety Report named the four next cities the same day. [Not a Tesla App](https://notateslaapp.com/news/4867/tesla-q3-2026-earnings-call-recap-everything-you-need-to-know), [Basenor](https://www.basenor.com/blogs/news/tesla-names-next-4-robotaxi-cities-las-vegas-phoenix-jacksonville-san-antonio)
- 2026-10-28: A Phoenix guide reported no announcement and no public rides in Arizona. [DockDuty](https://dockduty.com/blog/tesla-robotaxi-phoenix.html)
- 2026-08-20: Nevada approved Tesla for up to 5,000 vehicles in Clark County. The rules say service must begin within 120 days of the permit being issued, and only after inspections, insurance and filed rates are in place. 120 days from August 20 is about December 18; that is my own calculation, and the clock may start later if the permit was issued after the approval. Tesla's Cybercab engineer said it would not deploy 5,000 vehicles soon. An earlier report said an initial approval capped the fleet at 10 vehicles on the Strip corridor. [GovTech](https://www.govtech.com/transportation/tesla-waymo-uber-driverless-rides-greenlighted-in-las-vegas), [Drive Tesla](https://driveteslacanada.ca/robotaxi/tesla-las-vegas-robotaxi-permit-10-vehicles/), [Tesla Oracle](https://www.teslaoracle.com/2026/08/21/tesla-tsla-obtains-approval-for-robotaxi-service-in-nevada-including-las-vegas/)
- 2026-06-23: More gold Tesla robotaxi vehicles were spotted around Las Vegas, and Tesla had applied for its Nevada permit. [CDC Gaming](https://cdcgaming.com/brief/tesla-robotaxi-appears-to-be-gearing-up-for-las-vegas-launch/)
- 2026-04: About 60 robotaxi-spec Model Ys were seen staged in Phoenix. Tesla has an Arizona ride-hail (TNC) permit from November 2025 and has filed a first-responder plan in Arizona. [Not a Tesla App](https://www.notateslaapp.com/news/3923/tesla-begins-staging-for-robotaxi-launch-in-phoenix), [Basenor](https://www.basenor.com/blogs/news/tesla-robotaxi-expansion-60-model-ys-spotted-in-phoenix)
- 2026-01-29: Tesla targeted seven cities, including Phoenix and Las Vegas, for the first half of 2026. Phoenix and Las Vegas missed that target. [AZFamily](https://www.azfamily.com/2026/01/29/tesla-roll-out-self-driving-robotaxi-service-phoenix-this-year/)

## 4. Base rates
- Five of the seven cities targeted for the first half of 2026 have launched: Dallas and Houston in April, Miami in early July, Orlando and Tampa in late July. Phoenix and Las Vegas have each slipped more than five months past that target.
- San Antonio went from named to live in 19 days. Phoenix and Las Vegas have been "Coming soon" for about 27 days so far.
- Tesla launches have bunched together: two Texas cities in the first two weeks of November.
- The last six weeks of 2026 is a short window, but Tesla has a habit of launching just before year-end deadlines (Austin's ride-only Robotaxi launch hit its June 2025 target).

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "Which states will robotaxi be offered to this year?" (as of 2026-11-17): Arizona 49%, Nevada 41%, Florida 90%, California 3%. This seems to be about Tesla, but Florida at 90% is odd when Florida is already live, so the market's definition may differ (for example, it may require driverless rides or Cybercab). Check the market's rules before relying on it.
- Kalshi has Waymo operating in Las Vegas before 2027 at 63%. That sits awkwardly with ChargePort's claim, which I could not verify, that Waymo started paid Las Vegas rides on 2026-09-14.
- Polymarket has Tesla launching robotaxis in California by Dec 31 at 7%. This is not directly relevant.
- I found no market on Tesla in Phoenix or Las Vegas specifically, on Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-12-18: the likely end of Nevada's 120-day window to start service, by my calculation. Missing it could mean asking for an extension or risking the permit.
- December 2026: Cybercab customer deliveries begin "in select cities". A pilot letting private Model Y owners join the Robotaxi fleet in Austin is also planned.
- Late December 2026: Tesla's stated hope of reaching "more cities towards the end of the year", and a possible push to show progress before Q4 deliveries are reported in early January.
- Possible approval steps in Arizona (ADOT engagement was described as the gating item) and Clark County airport approval. Neither is required for a basic launch.

Neither city had Tesla Robotaxi service as of mid-November 2026. Both have been listed as "Coming soon" since 2026-10-21, and Tesla has given no launch date for either. I could not read the resolution page myself, so that status comes from third-party trackers.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-17: tesla.com/robotaxi and tesla.com/support/robotaxi both returned "403 Access Denied" to my tools. I could not read either page or find any data file behind them. [tesla.com/robotaxi](https://www.tesla.com/robotaxi)
- 2026-11-09 (tracker): Tesla's pages reportedly list Las Vegas, Phoenix and Jacksonville as "Coming soon", and have since 2026-10-21. Live cities are Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, San Antonio, Miami, Orlando, Tampa, plus the SF Bay Area with a safety driver. [thechargeport](https://thechargeport.com/robotaxi-tracker)
- Basenor's tracker shows Las Vegas as "Announced" and Phoenix as "Preparations Underway", with no launch dates. [basenor tracker](https://www.basenor.com/pages/tesla-robotaxi-tracker)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet.
- Las Vegas is the more advanced of the two on paper:
  - Nevada issued an interim permit on 2026-07-27, capped at 10 vehicles, limited to the Strip and 45 mph, with no airport pickups. [Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/08/17/tesla-nevada-robotaxi-permit-10-vehicles-las-vegas/), [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/14/tesla-sought-permit-for-5000-robotaxis-in-las-vegas-it-got-10)
  - Some outlets report a full permit on 2026-08-20 for up to 5,000 vehicles in Clark County. [frunklab](https://www.frunklab.com/news/robotaxi-las-vegas-nevada-approval)
  - Sources conflict on which permit terms apply now. I could not check the state's official docket (reported as 26-05015).
- Phoenix: Tesla reportedly holds an Arizona ride-hail permit from November 2025. About 60 robotaxi-spec Model Ys were reported staged in the area. There is no launch date. [dockduty](https://dockduty.com/blog/tesla-robotaxi-phoenix.html), [lightmytesla](https://lightmytesla.com/news/tesla-robotaxi-phoenix-expansion-june-2026)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: Tesla expanded its Miami service area to about 59 sq mi. Cybercab orders opened at $29,990, with deliveries from December in select service areas, Texas at first. [Teslarati](https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-doubled-miami-robotaxi-geofence/), [Motor1](https://www.motor1.com/news/815563/tesla-cybercab-robotaxi-limits/)
- 2026-11-16: Zoox robotaxis became available on Uber in Las Vegas, a competitor, not Tesla. [elaragueno](https://elaragueno.com.ve/zoox-incorpora-sus-taxis-autonomos-a-uber-en-las-vegas-para-competir-con-waymo-y-tesla/)
- 2026-11-09: San Antonio launched. It is the first of the four cities named on 2026-10-21 to go live, about 19 days after being named. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi)
- 2026-11-02: Fort Worth launched. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_Robotaxi)
- 2026-10-21: In its first Robotaxi Safety Report and on the Q3 call, Tesla named Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville and San Antonio as next cities, without dates. The CFO said "some other cities" by end of 2026. [Basenor](https://www.basenor.com/blogs/news/tesla-names-next-4-robotaxi-cities-las-vegas-phoenix-jacksonville-san-antonio), [TeslaNorth](https://teslanorth.com/2026/10/21/tesla-q3-2026-call-takeaways/)
- Possible Las Vegas deadline: Nevada rule NAC 706B.360 reportedly requires a permit holder to start operating within 120 days of the permit's issue date unless the authority allows otherwise. Counting from 2026-07-27 or 2026-08-20 gives about 2026-11-24 to 2026-12-18. The rule does not define what counts as "beginning operations", and the dates are a third party's calculation. [cybercab.news](https://www.cybercab.news/article/policy-nevada-120-day-robotaxi-clock-oct5)

## 4. Base rates
- Tesla often misses its own robotaxi timelines:
  - In January 2026 it targeted seven new cities, including Phoenix and Las Vegas, for the first half of 2026. Both slipped. [Tesery](https://www.tesery.com/blogs/news/tesla-confirms-aggressive-robotaxi-expansion-to-seven-major-us-cities-in-first-half-of-2026)
  - Phoenix has been "Preparations Underway" in the April and July 2026 shareholder updates. [thechargeport](https://thechargeport.com/robotaxi-tracker)
- Launch pace in 2026 has been steady: Dallas and Houston (04-18), Miami (07-03), Orlando and Tampa (07-21), Fort Worth (11-02), San Antonio (11-09).
- Every launch so far, apart from the safety-driver Bay Area, has been in Texas or Florida. No western state outside California has gone live.
- From "Coming soon" to live took about 19 days for San Antonio. Las Vegas, Phoenix and Jacksonville have been waiting about 27 days so far.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "Which states will robotaxi be offered to this year?" (before 2027-01-01), on 2026-11-17: Arizona 49%, Nevada 41%, Florida 90%, Georgia 17%, California 3%. This appears to track Tesla. I did not check the contract's exact wording, so it may resolve on other criteria, for example a state rather than the city, or a different source.
- Polymarket, Tesla robotaxi in California by Dec 31: 7%, which is not directly relevant.
- Manifold, Tesla fully driverless in 10+ US metros beyond Austin by 2027-08-01: 63%.
- I found no market on exactly this Las Vegas and Phoenix question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-11-24 to 2026-12-18: the possible Nevada 120-day deadline for Las Vegas.
- December 2026: Cybercab customer deliveries begin, and Musk says a pilot letting private Model Y owners join the fleet in Austin could start. [ixbt](https://www.ixbt.com/news/2026/11/17/tesla-budet-rabotat-poka-xoziain-otdyxaet-pilotnaia-programma-startuet-uze-v-dekabre-2026.html)
- A Jacksonville launch would show whether the "Coming soon" cities are moving forward.
- Year-end: Tesla's stated aim of "some other cities" by end of 2026. A Q4 update would only come in late January 2027, after resolution.
- What counts: a city still showing "Coming soon" on 12-31 resolves as no service.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 6 weeks, from 2026-11-17 to the 2026-12-31 snapshot of Tesla's Robotaxi portal.

(b) Status quo: Both Phoenix and Las Vegas have been listed as "Coming soon" since 2026-10-21, and neither has public rides. If nothing changes, the answer is "In neither city."

(c) Base rates:
- Five of the seven cities Tesla targeted for the first half of 2026 launched, but Phoenix and Las Vegas have slipped more than five months.
- San Antonio went from named to live in 19 days. Phoenix and Las Vegas are at 27 days and counting, which suggests they face specific obstacles.
- Tesla often launches in clusters and pushes to show progress by year-end.
- A six-week window for a city that has slipped repeatedly usually gives a launch chance of roughly 30-45%.

(d) Strongest evidence:
- 2026-11-17 Kalshi state markets: Arizona 49%, Nevada 41%. These are close proxies but not exact. The Florida price of 90% suggests the market's definition may differ from this question's.
- 2026-08-20: Nevada approved Tesla in Clark County. Service must start within 120 days of the permit being issued, which is about mid-to-late December if the clock started on approval. This creates a deadline that pushes toward a Las Vegas launch.
- 2026-04: About 60 robotaxi-spec Model Ys were staged in Phoenix. Tesla has held an Arizona ride-hail (TNC) permit since November 2025, but ADOT engagement was described as the gating step.
- 2026-10-21: Tesla said more cities could follow "towards the end of the year", without dates for either city.
- Tesla is expanding quickly: San Antonio, Fort Worth and a larger Miami area all came in November.

(e) Unexpected outcome: Tesla launches Las Vegas with a small fleet just before the Nevada permit deadline while Phoenix stays stuck on ADOT, giving "Las Vegas not Phoenix". Alternatively, both launch in a single December batch alongside Jacksonville.

How I got here: I started from the status quo of neither city. The Kalshi prices, after discounting for the definition mismatch, put each city at roughly 38-42%. Launches in the two cities are strongly correlated because Tesla tends to batch them. That leaves about 50% on neither. I put slightly more on Phoenix than on Las Vegas, matching Kalshi's order, though the Nevada deadline partly offsets that.

Option_A: 0.15
Option_B: 0.12
Option_C: 0.23
Option_D: 0.50

(a) **Time left:** About six weeks. The outcome is fixed by Tesla's Robotaxi page status on December 31, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** Both cities are listed as "Coming soon", which does not count. So the status quo outcome is "In neither city."

(c) **Base rates:**
- Tesla has missed its first-half 2026 target for both cities by more than five months.
- Five of the seven cities targeted for the first half of 2026 have launched, and all of those launched late. The two outliers are still pending.
- Newly named cities can launch fast. San Antonio went live 19 days after it was named on October 21.
- Tesla launches tend to bunch together, often near end-of-period deadlines.
- From this, the chance of any given pending city launching within six weeks is roughly 30-45%.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- October 21, 2026: Tesla named Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville and San Antonio as the next cities. San Antonio launched November 9. Fort Worth launched November 2.
- August 20, 2026: Nevada approved Tesla to operate in Clark County. Service must begin within 120 days of the permit being issued, which works out to around mid-to-late December. That creates pressure to launch in Las Vegas, but an extension is possible.
- Phoenix: Tesla has held an Arizona TNC permit since November 2025, and about 60 vehicles were staged in April 2026. Yet nothing has launched, and approval from ADOT is reportedly the gating item.
- Q3 call: Tesla spoke of "more cities towards the end of the year."
- Kalshi, November 17, 2026: Arizona 49%, Nevada 41%. This is the closest market, but it is thin and its Florida price is strange, so I give it only moderate weight.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** Tesla rushes Las Vegas live in mid-December to satisfy the Nevada 120-day clause, possibly with a tiny Strip-corridor fleet, while Phoenix slips into 2027 over ADOT issues. Or the reverse: Phoenix launches alongside a year-end push while Nevada inspections or insurance filings delay Las Vegas.

**Reasoning:** I start from Kalshi's roughly 45% per city and shade down slightly, because Phoenix has been staged for months without launching and the status quo is neither. That gives about 41% for Phoenix and 37% for Las Vegas. The two launches are positively correlated, since Tesla tends to make year-end batch announcements, so I put "both" at about 23%.

Option_A: 0.17
Option_B: 0.13
Option_C: 0.23
Option_D: 0.47

(a) **Time left:** About 6 weeks, from 2026-11-17 to 2026-12-31. The outcome will be known at the end of December.

(b) **Status quo:** Both cities are listed as "Coming soon" on Tesla's site, which does not count. If nothing changes, the answer is "In neither city".

(c) **Base rates:**
- Five of the seven cities targeted for the first half of 2026 have launched. Phoenix and Las Vegas each slipped more than five months past that target.
- Of the four cities named on 2026-10-21, San Antonio launched within 19 days. The other three have been "Coming soon" for about four weeks.
